problem: Combine simulation kinematic priors with human-video visual priors before adapting a bimanual manipulation policy using limited real-robot demonstrations.
contribution: SimHum co-trains task-aligned simulation and human data through source-specific action/vision adaptors around a shared diffusion-transformer policy, then recombines real-vision and robot-action modules for finetuning.
algorithm: Human44Dhand-pose and robot actions use separate encoders/decoders; simulation/human images use source adaptors. Optimize a mixture-weighted diffusion objective through batch composition, then keep the human-stream visual adaptor and simulation-trained robot-action modules for end-to-end real finetuning.
observations: Task-aligned camera images and robot/human state representations. Source robot and simulator use identical URDFs; self-collected human views are deliberately aligned with the robot head camera, not unconstrained internet clips.
actions: Source-specific robot controls versus44Dhuman wrist/fingertip coordinates. Human pose labels are training targets and cannot be sent directly to a robot actuator interface.
embodiment_and_data: Four bimanual tabletop tasks. Per task500simulated and500human demonstrations, plus80real episodes for every compared method. Human data spans12scenarios; source collection factors include objects, distractors, lights, backgrounds and initial positions.
experiments: Per configuration ID40trials and OOD20trials per task, with held-out visual factors outside source data/randomization. Main cells are single trained policies with trial-level standard errors; separate second-seed checks are mentioned. Ablations test adaptors, pose loss, mixture ratio and data scales.
baselines: Real-only, human-pretrained and simulation-pretrained variants with matched architecture/final real data. Collection-time studies exclude simulation generation from charged budgets, so they are not total compute/energy/wall-clock cost comparisons.

quantitative_result.value: Main four-task OOD average62.5% with80real episodes/task,53.7percentage points above Real-only. Separate StackBowlsTwo ablation reports75.0±9.7% versus40.0±11.0% without vision adaptors. Trial standard errors are not uncertainty across many independent training seeds.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p9 Conclusion; p8 Table1; p6 Evaluation Protocol

limitations: Same task set across sources and deliberately aligned URDF/views restrict claims of arbitrary embodiment/video transfer. Four tabletop tasks do not cover wild manipulation, humanoid/mobile domains or a general foundation-policy recipe. Remaining contact timing and coordination errors motivate additional feedback.
code_and_license: Primary fulltext/appendix references examined; executable source, human-data permissions and code/model licenses not independently audited. No local SimHum implementation or physical result is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Relevant to the proposed simulation/human/robot study only after real kinematic/camera contracts and measurable actions are established. An overview-only Pi camera and unmeasured controller state do not automatically satisfy the source alignment assumptions; report all acquisition and compute budgets separately.
